why: Instead of enumerating subarrays, count for each element how many subarrays it is the minimum of: (i - previous smaller index) * (next smaller-or-equal index - i). Previous and next smaller elements come from a monotonic stack. It teaches the contribution technique.
hints: Turn it around: for a fixed arr[i], in how many subarrays is it the minimum?
In every subarray that starts after the previous smaller element and ends before the next smaller element: left choices times right choices.
Find prev (strictly smaller) and next (smaller or equal) with a monotonic stack, sum arr[i] * (i - prev) * (next - i), take mod 10^9+7. O(n).
pitfalls: With equal values, use a strict bound on one side and a non-strict one on the other, or subarrays with tied minimums are counted twice or not at all.
Apply the modulo to the final sum (or as you go); the raw sum can be very large.
